historicalContracts.name: QuotaManager
historicalContracts.note: Defined per-token withdrawal limits enforced on the bridge outflow path; compromise/mutation sets quotas to zero and freezes all bridge withdrawals (or removes the rate-limit backstop during an exploit).

historicalContracts.name: TaikoSP1Verifier
historicalContracts.note: Live SP1 gating router with trustedPrograms vkeys in the batch proof path; compromise or a malicious trusted-program hash accepts fake validity proofs, finalizing a forged state root and draining the bridge.

historicalContracts.name: L1SharedAddressManager
historicalContracts.note: Resolved trusted addresses for Bridge/SignalService/Vaults (remapping acts as an upgrade); compromise points the bridge at a malicious SignalService to forge withdrawal messages and drain escrows.

historicalContracts.name: Bridge
historicalContracts.note: L2-side message bridge in the deposit/withdrawal validation path; compromise mints forged L2->L1 messages that release L1 escrow funds.

historicalContracts.name: ERC20Vault
historicalContracts.note: L2-side token vault paired with the L1 ERC20Vault escrow; compromise emits fraudulent burn/withdraw messages that unlock the L1 escrow's tokens.

historicalContracts.name: SignalService
historicalContracts.note: L2-side signal/state-root registry used to validate cross-chain messages; compromise attests fake signals/state roots enabling forged withdrawals in both directions.

historicalContracts.name: Anchor
historicalContracts.note: L2 anchor system contract syncing L1 state roots into the L2 (withdrawal-validation input); compromise injects a fake L1 state root, allowing forged deposit messages to mint/withdraw on L2.

historicalContracts.name: ForcedInclusionStore
historicalContracts.note: Mandatory dependency of TaikoWrapper.proposeBatch (forced-inclusion queue); a critical mutation making its due/consume checks revert bricks all batch proposals, halting the chain and freezing bridged funds.

historicalContracts.name: TaikoL1
historicalContracts.note: Core rollup entrypoint and L2 state machine holding bonds and verified state roots; compromise finalizes an arbitrary state transition, letting the attacker prove fake withdrawals against all bridge escrows.

historicalContracts.name: ProverSet
historicalContracts.note: Taiko team operator proxy for proposing/proving; it holds only its own TAIKO bonds and its proofs are still checked by the verifiers, so compromise risks operator funds, not user funds.

historicalContracts.name: Risc0VerifierGateway
historicalContracts.note: Live entry contract for RISC Zero batch proofs in the Pacaya multi-proof path; compromise routes to a malicious verifier that accepts fake proofs, finalizing forged state and draining the bridge.

historicalContracts.name: TaikoWrapper
historicalContracts.note: Sole entry point for block/batch proposals into the inbox (enforcing forced inclusion); a critical mutation that reverts proposals halts the chain and freezes all bridged funds.

historicalContracts.name: VerifierGateway
historicalContracts.note: Multi-proof gateway that routed each proof type to its verifier (ComposeVerifier); compromise redirects any proof type to an always-true verifier, finalizing fake state and draining the bridge.

historicalContracts.name: SP1VerifierGateway
historicalContracts.note: Live entry contract for SP1 batch proofs in the Pacaya multi-proof path; compromise accepts fake SP1 proofs, finalizing forged state roots and draining the bridge.

historicalContracts.name: PreconfRouter
historicalContracts.note: Exclusive proposal route into TaikoWrapper for whitelisted preconf operators; a critical mutation that rejects all proposals halts batch production, freezing bridged funds.

historicalContracts.name: ProverSet
historicalContracts.note: Taiko team operator proxy for proposing/proving; holds only its own bonds and its outputs are validated by the verifier contracts, so no path to user funds.

historicalContracts.name: GuardianMinorityProver
historicalContracts.note: Second-highest-tier verifier (guardian minority) that overrides SGX/ZK proofs; compromise proves a fake state transition that finalizes unless the full guardian tier contests in time, enabling bridge drain.

historicalContracts.name: L1RollupAddressManager
historicalContracts.note: Resolved TaikoL1's trusted rollup addresses including tier verifiers (remapping acts as an upgrade); compromise swaps in a malicious verifier so fake proofs finalize and drain the bridge.

historicalContracts.name: SgxVerifier
historicalContracts.note: Live SGX-tier proof verifier in the tier system; compromise (e.g. registering a rogue attested instance) proves fake state transitions that finalize if uncontested, draining the bridge.

historicalContracts.name: GuardianProver
historicalContracts.note: Top-tier verifier: guardian multisig proofs override all other tiers uncontested and it held the chain_watchdog pause; compromise finalizes arbitrary fake state (bridge drain) or pauses proving (freeze).
